book: Nancy Caroline · Chapter 50 · Medical Incident Command
title: Mass-Casualty Incidents: Command and Triage

slides.title: Today's lesson
slides.body:
As an EMR you size up a scene, then give one patient everything. Today, as a PCP:

  1. Recognize an MCI and how the incident command system is built
  2. Know the medical branch jobs, and what to do if you're first on scene
  3. Triage fast with START and JumpSTART, then transport in order

Textbook: Chapter 50, PDF pages 4155–4194
slides.say: Welcome back. As EMRs, you're used to sizing up a scene and then giving one patient everything you have. A mass-casualty incident turns that upside down: there are more patients than resources, so the goal becomes the greatest good for the greatest number. As a PCP, you may be first on scene, even incident commander or triage officer. There's no BC protocol for this, so today we follow the textbook: how command is organized, the jobs in the medical branch, and fast triage with START and JumpSTART.
slides.sayZh: 欢迎回来。作为 EMR，你们习惯先评估现场，然后把全部精力给一个病人。大规模伤亡事件把这一切颠倒过来：病人比资源多，目标变成为最多的人做最大的好事。作为 PCP，你可能第一个到场，甚至担任事故指挥官或分诊官。这部分 BC 没有流程，所以今天按教科书来：指挥体系怎么组织；医疗分部里的各个岗位；以及用 START 和 JumpSTART 快速分诊。

slides.title: What makes it an MCI?
slides.body:
Patients outnumber the first responders' resources

  • No fixed number: a crash with several critical patients can be one
  • Closed: patients in one place, no new ones (a bus rollover)
  • Open: patients not all found, or more keep coming
  • A closed incident can suddenly become open
slides.say: What makes an incident a mass-casualty incident, or MCI? It's not a set number. An MCI is any event where the patients outnumber the resources of the first responders. In a small town with one ambulance, a crash with several critical patients is an MCI. Next, decide whether it's closed or open. A closed incident has all its patients in one place, and no new ones are expected, like a bus that rolled over. An open incident still has patients you haven't found, or keeps producing new ones, like a shooting, a flood, or wildfire smoke reaching a town. And a closed incident can suddenly turn open, so keep reassessing.
slides.sayZh: 什么样的事件算大规模伤亡事件，也就是 MCI？没有固定人数。只要病人数超过首批到场者的资源，就是 MCI。在只有一辆救护车的小镇，一起有几名危重伤员的车祸就是 MCI。接着判断它是封闭的还是开放的。封闭事件的病人都集中在一处，不会再增加，比如一辆翻车的大巴。开放事件还有没找到的病人，或者还在不断产生新病人，比如枪击、洪水，或者林火烟雾飘进城镇。封闭事件也可能突然变成开放事件，所以要不断重新评估。

slides.title: The incident command system
slides.body:
• Plain language, no codes; one structure that scales
  • Span of control 3–7, ideal 1:5; more than 7? Split
  • Incident commander: objectives and plan; COMMAND vest
  • Command staff: safety (can stop work), public info, liaison
  • General staff: operations, planning, logistics, finance
  • Unified command (many agencies) vs single (one agency)
slides.say: The incident command system, or ICS, gives every agency the same structure and plain-language job titles, with no codes, and it grows or shrinks with the event. It prevents freelancing, which means units acting on their own. Span of control is three to seven people per supervisor, ideally five; with more than seven, split the tasks. At the top, the incident commander sets the objectives and the plan; look for the COMMAND vest. The command staff are the safety officer, who can stop any operation, the public information officer for the media, and the liaison officer for other agencies. The general staff runs operations, planning, logistics and finance. Big multi-agency events use unified command; small ones, single command.
slides.sayZh: 事故指挥系统，简称 ICS，让所有机构使用同一套结构和明语岗位名称，不用代码，并能随事件大小扩展或收缩。它能防止各自为政，也就是各单位自行其是。管理幅度是每个督导管三到七人，最好五人；超过七人就要拆分任务。最上面是事故指挥官，负责制定目标和计划，认准写着 COMMAND 的背心。指挥参谋包括：安全官，有权叫停任何行动；新闻官，对接媒体；联络官，对接其他机构。一般参谋管行动、计划、后勤、财务四个部。大型多机构事件用统一指挥，小型事件用单一指挥。

slides.title: First on scene: three questions
slides.body:
1. What do I have? Hazards, location, number of patients
  2. What do I need to do? Safety → stabilize the incident → protect property
  3. What do I need? More units, air, rescue, hazmat

Then report, establish command early, and request resources.
slides.say: If you're the first crew to arrive, keep it simple and keep asking three questions. What do I have? Check for hazards like fuel, power lines or chemicals, and warn others; confirm the location, and estimate the number of patients. What do I need to do? The priorities, in order, are safety, then stabilizing the incident, then protecting property and the environment. Safety means you and your partner first; an injured rescuer only adds to the patient count. What do I need? More ambulances, air, a rescue unit, or a hazmat team right away if there are hazardous materials. Then report, establish command, and request resources.
slides.sayZh: 如果你是第一个到场的车组，就简单点，反复问自己三个问题。我面对的是什么？查有没有燃油、电线、化学品之类的危险并警告其他人，确认地点，估计病人数量。我要做什么？优先顺序是：安全，然后稳定事态，然后保护财产和环境。安全首先是你和搭档；救援人员一受伤，只会让伤员更多。我需要什么？更多救护车、空中救护、救援队；有危险品就立即叫危险品队。然后向调度报告、建立指挥、请求资源。

slides.q: You're the first ambulance at a highway pileup. About 15 people are hurt, some walking, and fuel is leaking from one car. No one else has arrived. What do you do first?
options: Start treating the most seriously injured patient you can reach
Warn others about the fuel, report to dispatch, establish command and request resources
Load the two worst patients and leave for the hospital right away
Wait in the ambulance until a supervisor arrives to take command
slides.say: Let's pause for a question. You're the first ambulance at a highway pileup. About fifteen people are hurt, some of them walking, and fuel is leaking from one car. No one else has arrived. What do you do first? A, start treating the most seriously injured patient you can reach. B, warn others about the fuel, report to dispatch, establish command and request resources. C, load the two worst patients and leave for the hospital right away. D, wait in the ambulance until a supervisor arrives to take command. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 停一下考考你。你是第一辆到达高速公路连环相撞现场的救护车，约十五人受伤，有些人能走，一辆车在漏油，其他人都还没到。你第一步做什么？A 开始救治你能接触到的伤得最重的病人；B 警告他人注意漏油，向调度报告，建立指挥并请求资源；C 把最重的两个病人装车，立即去医院；D 在车里等主管到场接管指挥。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. The first crew sizes up the scene, warns others about hazards, reports, establishes command early, and calls for resources. A makes you one provider for one patient while nobody runs the scene. C takes away the only ambulance before anyone knows how many patients there are. D wastes the most important minutes; the first paramedic on scene can take command.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。第一个到场的车组要评估现场、警告他人注意危险、向调度报告、尽早建立指挥并请求资源。A 让你变成只照顾一个病人的人，而整个现场无人指挥。C 在没人知道有多少病人之前就带走了唯一一辆救护车。D 浪费了最关键的几分钟；第一个到场的急救员就可以担任指挥。

slides.title: The medical branch
slides.body:
RoleMain job
Triage officerCount and sort everyone; no treatment until all are triaged
Treatment officerTreatment area by priority; secondary triage
Transport officerTalks to hospitals; tracks each patient and unit
Staging officerHolds arriving units away from the scene
Rehab officerRest, fluids, food for rescuers; watches for stress
slides.say: When an incident has a big medical side, the IC names a medical branch or group leader, who runs triage, treatment and transport. The triage officer counts and sorts every patient, and the hardest rule is this: don't start standard treatment until everyone is triaged. The treatment officer sets up the treatment area, with a section for each priority, and makes sure secondary triage happens. The transport officer talks with hospitals and records which patient left in which vehicle to which hospital. The staging officer keeps arriving ambulances away from the scene until they're assigned. And in a long event, the rehabilitation officer gives rescuers rest, fluids and food, and watches them for signs of stress.
slides.sayZh: 当事件的医疗部分很重时，IC 会指定一名医疗分部或医疗组负责人，统管分诊、处置和转运。分诊官负责清点所有病人并排序，最难的一条规矩是：所有人分诊完之前，不要开始常规处置。处置官设立处置区，按优先级分区，并确保进行二次分诊。转运官与医院沟通，记录哪个病人坐哪辆车去了哪家医院。集结官让陆续到达的救护车停在远离现场的地方，接到指派才进去。在长时间事件中，康复官为救援人员提供休息、饮水和食物，并观察他们有没有应激表现。

slides.title: Four triage colours: IDME
slides.body:
Immediate · redairway or breathing, uncontrolled bleeding, shock, ↓ LOC, severe burns1st
Delayed · yellowmajor bone or joint injuries, back injuries, burns without airway problems2nd
Minimal · greenwalking wounded, minor injuries3rd

Expectant · black: dead, or survival unlikely (cardiac arrest, major open brain injury). Last.
slides.say: Most systems use four colours, remembered as IDME, which is also the order of treatment and transport. Immediate, red: problems with airway or breathing, uncontrolled bleeding, shock, decreased mental status, severe burns, or open chest or abdominal wounds. Delayed, yellow: they need care, but it can wait a little, like major or multiple bone and joint injuries, back injuries, or burns without airway problems. Minimal, green: the walking wounded, with minor injuries. Expectant, black: dead, or so badly injured that survival is unlikely, like cardiac arrest or a major open brain injury; with very limited resources, respiratory arrest too. Every tag needs at least a unique number and the category.
slides.sayZh: 多数系统用四种颜色，口诀是 IDME，也就是处置和转运的顺序。立即，红色：气道或呼吸有问题、出血控制不住、休克、意识下降、严重烧伤，或开放性胸腹部伤口。延迟，黄色：需要处置但可以稍等，比如严重或多处骨关节损伤、背部损伤、没有气道问题的烧伤。轻微，绿色：能走动的轻伤者。期待，黑色：已经死亡，或伤势重到几乎不可能存活，比如心脏骤停或严重开放性颅脑损伤；资源非常有限时，呼吸停止也归这一类。每张标签至少要有唯一编号和分类。

slides.title: START triage, step by step
slides.body:
Walk→Breathe→Rate→Radial pulse→Commands
  • Walks to the meeting point = green
  • Not breathing → open airway: still nothing = black; breathes = red
  • Breathing over 30 = red
  • No radial pulse = red
  • Can't follow a simple command = red; can = yellow
slides.say: START stands for Simple Triage And Rapid Treatment. First, call out: if you can hear me and can walk, go to that spot. Everyone who walks there is green. Then go to each patient who can't walk. Not breathing? Open the airway with a simple manoeuvre. If they still don't breathe, they're black; if they start breathing, they're red, so put them in the recovery position and move on. Breathing faster than thirty? Red. Next, check the radial pulse; if it's absent, they're red. Finally, ask them to do something simple, like show you three fingers. Can't do it? Red. Can do it? Yellow. That's it: walk, breathe, rate, pulse, commands.
slides.sayZh: START 的意思是简单分诊与快速处置。第一步，大声喊：能听见我说话、能走路的，到那边去。走过去的人都是绿色。然后逐个查看不能走的病人。没有呼吸？用简单手法开放气道：仍不呼吸就是黑色；开始呼吸就是红色，摆成复原卧位，接着看下一个。呼吸每分钟超过三十次？红色。接着摸桡动脉，摸不到就是红色。最后让他做个简单动作，比如伸出三根手指：做不到，红色；做得到，黄色。就这么几步：能走、呼吸、频率、脉搏、听令。

slides.title: JumpSTART: children are different
slides.body:
• Age < 8, or looks < 45 kg
  • Not breathing? Check pulse first: none = black
  • Pulse, still not breathing after airway opened: 5 rescue breaths
  • Breathing < 15 or > 45 = red
  • No distal pulse = red
  • AVPU: unresponsive, posturing, or can't localize pain = red
slides.say: Children aren't small adults, so for children younger than eight, or who look under forty-five kilograms, use JumpSTART. Children too young to walk go straight to the treatment area for secondary triage. If a child isn't breathing, feel for a pulse first. No pulse means black. With a pulse, open the airway; if they still don't breathe, give five rescue breaths, because in children cardiac arrest usually starts as respiratory arrest. Still not breathing? Black. A breathing rate under fifteen or over forty-five is red. No distal pulse is red. For mental status, use modified AVPU: unresponsive, posturing, or unable to localize pain is red; alert, or localizing or withdrawing from pain, is yellow.
slides.sayZh: 儿童不是缩小版的成人，所以八岁以下或看起来不到四十五公斤的孩子，用 JumpSTART。还不会走路的小孩，直接尽快送到处置区做二次分诊。孩子没有呼吸时，先摸脉搏：没有脉搏就是黑色。有脉搏就开放气道；仍不呼吸，给五次人工呼吸，因为儿童心脏骤停通常由呼吸停止引起。还不呼吸？黑色。呼吸频率低于十五或高于四十五，红色。摸不到远端脉搏，红色。神志用改良 AVPU：无反应、出现姿势反射、或不能定位疼痛，红色；清醒、能定位疼痛或躲避疼痛，黄色。

slides.q: You're a PCP working as triage officer at a train derailment with about 40 patients. A man can't walk; he's breathing 34 times a minute, with a weak radial pulse. Your partner hands you an IV start kit. What do you do?
options: Start an IV and a fluid bolus, then continue triage
Tag him red and move on to the next patient
Tag him yellow, since he still has a radial pulse
Stay with him and give TXA before moving on
slides.say: Now a PCP decision. You're a PCP working as triage officer at a train derailment with about forty patients. A man can't walk. He's breathing thirty-four times a minute, with a weak radial pulse. Your partner hands you an IV start kit. What do you do? A, start an IV and a fluid bolus, then continue triage. B, tag him red and move on to the next patient. C, tag him yellow, since he still has a radial pulse. D, stay with him and give TXA before moving on. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来一道 PCP 决策题。火车出轨现场约四十名病人，你是担任分诊官的 PCP。一名男子不能行走，呼吸每分钟三十四次，桡动脉搏动微弱。搭档把静脉穿刺包递给你。你怎么做？A 先开静脉、补液，再继续分诊；B 给他贴红色标签，接着去看下一个病人；C 他还有桡动脉搏动，贴黄色；D 留下来给他用 TXA 再走。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. Breathing over thirty makes him red under START, so you tag him and move on. As triage officer, you don't start standard treatment until everyone is triaged, even with PCP skills like IV access and TXA. A and D spend your time on one patient while others wait unassessed. C is wrong: his breathing rate already makes him red.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。按 START，呼吸超过三十次就是红色，贴好标签就去看下一个。作为分诊官，在所有人分诊完之前不开始常规处置，哪怕你有静脉通路和 TXA 这些 PCP 技能。A 和 D 把时间花在一个病人身上，而其他人还在等着被评估。C 错在他的呼吸频率已经决定他是红色。

slides.title: Getting patients out
slides.body:
1. Red: two per ambulance until all are gone
  2. Yellow: two or three at a time
  3. Green: next; a bus can take them to a farther hospital
  4. Black, still alive: after the others
  • Bus: at least one paramedic or responder aboard; ambulance follows
  • Injured rescuer, or a panicking, disruptive patient: red, off site
slides.say: Transport follows the same order as triage. Red patients go two at a time per ambulance until all are gone. Then yellow, two or three at a time. Then the green, walking wounded. In a big event, a bus can carry them to a hospital farther away, so local hospitals aren't overwhelmed; put at least one paramedic or first responder on the bus, with an ambulance following in case someone gets worse. Expectant patients who are still alive come after that. Two special cases: a rescuer who is hurt or becomes ill is tagged red and moved off the site quickly, and so is a panicking, disruptive patient, because panic spreads.
slides.sayZh: 转运顺序和分诊顺序一样。红色病人每辆救护车两人，直到全部送走；然后是黄色，每次两到三人；然后是绿色的可行走伤员。大型事件中可以用大巴把他们送到较远的医院，以免本地医院被挤爆；车上至少要有一名急救员或第一响应者，后面跟一辆救护车，以防有人病情恶化。之后才轮到仍然活着的期待类病人。两种特殊情况：救援人员受伤或生病，贴红色标签并尽快撤离现场；惊慌失措、扰乱救援的病人也一样，因为恐慌会传染。

slides.title: What the PCP actually does
slides.body:
All licence levels (EMR + PCP)

  • Triage and tagging (book: START / JumpSTART)
  • Work in your assigned ICS role
  • Bleeding control: direct pressure, tourniquet
  • Oxygen to SpO₂ ≥ 94%

PCP adds (treatment area)

  • Reds waiting for transport = a time delay
  • BC hypovolemia: IV access, 20 mL/kg up to 2 L
  • Reassess every 500 mL; consider TXA

During primary triage, PCP skills wait.
slides.say: So what does the PCP actually do at an MCI? Every licence level triages and tags patients, with the book's START or JumpSTART system, works in an assigned ICS role, and gives basic lifesaving care: direct pressure, a tourniquet, and oxygen to ninety-four percent. The first paramedic on scene may even be incident commander until relieved face to face. The PCP difference shows up in the treatment area, where red patients may wait for an ambulance. BC's hypovolemia protocol lets the PCP act en route or when there's a time delay: IV access, twenty millilitres per kilogram up to two litres, reassessing every five hundred, and considering TXA. During primary triage, though, those skills wait.
slides.sayZh: 那么在 MCI 现场，PCP 实际做什么？所有执照级别都会用书中的 START 或 JumpSTART 系统分诊、贴标签，在指派的 ICS 岗位上工作，并做基本的救命处置：直接压迫、止血带、给氧到百分之九十四。第一个到场的急救员甚至可能先担任事故指挥官，直到有人当面接手。PCP 的不同体现在处置区，红色病人可能要在那里等救护车。BC 的低血容量流程允许 PCP 在途中或有时间延误时处置：建立静脉通路，每公斤二十毫升、最多两升，每五百毫升复评一次，并考虑 TXA。不过在初次分诊时，这些技能要先放一放。

slides.title: New for you as a PCP: watch out for
slides.body:
• New skills tempt you to treat during triage. Don't
  • After triage, report: total, number per colour, extrication, resources
  • Kids' numbers differ: 15–45, not 30; five rescue breaths
  • Secondary triage in the treatment area: patients change
  • Arriving later? Report to staging; wait for an assignment
  • Exposed to smoke, dust or chemicals? Get checked
slides.say: Here's what's new to watch for. First, your PCP skills will tempt you to start treating during primary triage. Don't: every minute with one patient is a minute others wait to be found. Second, after primary triage, report the total number of patients, the number in each colour, extrication needs, and the resources you need. Third, don't mix up the numbers: adults are red above thirty breaths a minute, children below fifteen or above forty-five, and children get five rescue breaths. Fourth, patients change, so secondary triage happens in the treatment area. If you arrive later, report to staging and wait for an assignment. And after smoke, dust or chemical exposure, get yourself checked.
slides.sayZh: 下面是你要注意的新问题。第一，PCP 技能会诱惑你在初次分诊时就开始处置。不要这样做：在一个病人身上多花的每一分钟，都是其他人多等的一分钟。第二，初次分诊后要报告：病人总数、每种颜色的人数、破拆需求和所需资源。第三，不要把数字搞混：成人呼吸超过每分钟三十次是红色，儿童是低于十五或高于四十五，而且儿童要给五次人工呼吸。第四，病情会变化，所以处置区要做二次分诊。如果你是后到的，先到集结区报到，等待指派。还有，接触过烟雾、粉尘或化学品后，要让自己接受检查。

slides.title: For the BC exam
slides.body:
The book's SALT triage allows quick lifesaving steps, including needle decompression and antidote auto-injectors. BC scope:

  • Needle decompression: not in EMR or PCP scope
  • Atropine and pralidoxime: not in EMR or PCP scope
  • Open chest wound: seal it; tension signs → lift a corner
  • Bleeding: tourniquet; wound packing, but not neck, chest or abdomen
slides.say: The book also describes SALT triage, which adds a fifth, grey category for patients not expected to survive with the resources available. SALT allows quick lifesaving steps during triage: bleeding control, opening the airway with two rescue breaths for children, needle decompression, and antidote auto-injectors. In BC, needle decompression is not in EMR or PCP scope, and neither are the nerve-agent antidotes atropine and pralidoxime. What you can do: seal an open chest wound, and if tension signs develop, lift a corner to let air out. Control bleeding with a tourniquet, or packing, but never pack the neck, chest or abdomen.
slides.sayZh: 书里还介绍了 SALT 分诊，它多出第五类灰色，指以现有资源预计救不活的病人。SALT 允许在分诊时做快速救命处置：止血、开放气道（儿童给两次人工呼吸）、针刺减压和自动注射解毒剂。在 BC，针刺减压不在 EMR 或 PCP 范围内，神经毒剂解毒剂阿托品和解磷定也不在。你能做的是：用封闭敷料封住开放性胸部伤口，出现张力征象时掀开一角放气；用止血带止血，或填塞止血，但颈部、胸部、腹部绝不填塞。

slides.title: Three things to remember
slides.body:
1. MCI = patients outnumber resources. First in: three questions, then command
  2. ICS: plain language, span of control 3–7, no freelancing
  3. START: walk, breathing > 30, radial pulse, commands. JumpSTART: 15–45, 5 breaths

Next: Chapter 51, Terrorism and CBRNE Events
slides.say: Three things to remember. One: an MCI is any incident where patients outnumber the first responders' resources. If you're first, ask what do I have, what do I need to do, and what do I need, then establish command. Two: ICS works because everyone uses plain language and the same structure, with three to seven people per supervisor and no freelancing. Three: START checks walking, breathing over thirty, radial pulse, and simple commands; JumpSTART changes the breathing range to fifteen to forty-five and adds five rescue breaths. Next class: Chapter 51, terrorism and CBRNE events. If anything was unclear, tap Ask. See you next class.
slides.sayZh: 收尾三句话。一，只要病人数超过首批到场者的资源，就是 MCI；如果你第一个到，就问：我面对什么、我要做什么、我需要什么，然后建立指挥。二，ICS 之所以有效，是因为大家用明语和同一套结构，每个督导管三到七人，不各自为政。三，START 看能否行走、呼吸是否超过三十、桡动脉、能否听令；JumpSTART 把呼吸范围改成十五到四十五，并加上五次人工呼吸。下节课是第五十一章，恐怖袭击与 CBRNE 事件。有不懂的点「Ask」。下节课见。
